courses.subtitle_en: Knit fabrics, T‑shirt design, printing, testing and sourcing in Sri Lanka — for a premium clothing brand
courses.language: Sinhala, with industry terms in English
courses.summary: A self-study course for someone entering the clothing trade who wants to build a premium T‑shirt brand that lasts. It starts with how Sri Lanka's export garment industry really works, then works through fibres and yarn, knit fabrics, lab testing to export standards, design and tech packs, screen printing and inks, production and AQL quality control, sourcing from Sri Lankan mills, factories and labs, and finally pricing, registration and a 90‑day launch plan.
courses.why: Export factories in Sri Lanka make world-class T‑shirts because of a process — nominated fabric, nominated inks, testing on every lot, sealed samples and final inspection — not because of a secret product. This course teaches that process at a size a new brand can afford.
outcomes: Read and write a fabric spec sheet: composition, yarn count, GSM, finishes, shrinkage and colourfastness targets
Choose the right knit (single jersey, interlock, pique, rib) and weight for each garment
Test fabric and garments — at home and at SGS, Intertek or Bureau Veritas — and read the report
Build a size chart and tech pack a factory can produce from without you in the room
Judge a print house: inks, curing, stretch and wash tests, common defects
Cost a T‑shirt, plan a production run and run an AQL 2.5 final inspection
Source fabric, trims, printing and factories in Sri Lanka, and negotiate around MOQs
Register the business, protect the brand name and launch in 90 days
audience: Someone starting a clothing brand in Sri Lanka who wants quality over volume
Anyone who has a friend or relative in a garment factory and wants to understand what they do
Small print shops and CMT units that want to serve premium customers
requirements: Reads Sinhala; comfortable with English technical terms in brackets
A few T‑shirts and fabric swatches to practise on
Time for the field exercises: Pettah, a factory visit, a print house, a lab quotation
includes: 9 modules, each with Sri Lanka examples and a practical exercise
10 self-marking quizzes — 60 questions — with explanations for every answer
6 copy‑paste templates: fabric spec sheet, lot acceptance sheet, PP checklist, AQL inspection sheet, supplier comparison, complaint log
A glossary of 60+ industry terms and a library of 150+ verified links to institutes, labs, mills, standards and suppliers
extras: ආකෘති සහ චෙක්ලිස්ට් — Templates and checklists

courses.subtitle_en: Tour guiding, homestays, experiences, itineraries, pricing, bookings and operations in Sri Lanka
courses.language: Sinhala, with tourism and digital terms in English
courses.level: Beginner — no degree or prior tourism experience needed
courses.summary: A Sinhala-first, practical course for someone who wants to start a small tourism business in Sri Lanka. It covers choosing a customer segment, designing local experiences, guiding and storytelling, homestay operations, itineraries and suppliers, pricing and commissions, online bookings and reviews, safety and service recovery, current registration paths, and a 90-day launch plan.
courses.why: Tourism businesses are often started with a vehicle, a spare room or local knowledge, but long-term reviews and profit come from repeatable operations. This course turns informal know-how into a simple system: a clear offer, accurate expectations, supplier confirmations, costing, safety checks, records and a feedback loop.
outcomes: Choose a specific tourism customer segment and write a clear value proposition
Design a half-day, full-day or small-stay experience with realistic timing, inclusions and a Plan B
Guide and tell stories without information overload or invented facts
Run a basic homestay room-ready, check-in and cleaning SOP
Build itineraries and a supplier network with written confirmations and backups
Price direct and commission-channel bookings without accidentally deleting the margin
Turn inquiries into bookings, collect genuine reviews and track profit by channel
Identify the current SLTDA registration path and execute a 90-day launch plan
audience: Sri Lankans who want to start a tour, local experience, homestay or trip-planning business
Drivers, guides and hosts who already help travellers informally and want a more professional system
Small accommodation and service businesses that want better bookings, reviews and operations
requirements: Reads Sinhala; basic English helps with tourism terms and foreign-guest communication
A smartphone and access to Google Maps/WhatsApp or equivalent tools
Time to do field exercises: test a route, talk to suppliers and run at least one dry run
includes: 9 practical modules with Sri Lankan examples and field exercises
A tourism glossary and official-source resource library for registration, visa, tax and training checks
